title: Seven Calls to Praise
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: Give thanks, call on his name, make known his deeds, sing, glory in his name, and seek his strength and his presence continually.
exhortation: The psalmist is bursting with exhortations to praise the Lord. In these four short verses I counted at least seven.

Give thanks to the Lord. What warms your heart more than recounting what you're grateful for? So much of life is spent focused inward on what we don't have, what we need, what we're trying to get. Even surrounded by wealth, we can focus on everything we lack. The psalmist says, give thanks. Remember all that you have.
Call upon his name. With a grateful heart, bring your petitions, your cares, your wants and your needs to the Lord.

Make known his deeds among the peoples. Tell of his wondrous works. Something stirs in you when you share with others what God has done in your life. It affects the person you're sharing with, and it affects your own soul.
Sing praises to him. This is why Jonathan and I are so passionate about beginning some part of your day with singing. It stirs your heart for the things of God.

Glory in his holy name. The Lord is set apart, altogether different from us. His glory shines through the universe: in the sun and moon, and in the faces of our children, our spouses, our friends and family.

Seek the Lord and his strength. Don't work in your own power. Work in the power of his Holy Spirit. And finally, seek his presence continually, so that our lives are lived before the face of God. Is your day unclear? In the presence of the Lord we receive clarity and see with spiritual eyes we didn't have before. So that's my prayer for us this morning: that we would give thanks, call on his name, make his deeds known, sing his praises, glory in his name, and seek his strength and his presence continually.
prayer: Lord, the commands you give are glorious and wonderful to obey. You have said, "Seek my face," and my heart says, "Your face, Lord, do I seek." Thank you for revealing yourself. Apart from your grace, I would never find you. But you came to us, opened our blinded eyes and poured out your grace so that we could see your glory. We are grateful.

As we go through our day, bring this scripture to mind. Giving you thanks is a gift to us: it builds up our hearts and gives us strength, joy and peace in you. Thank you that we can know your name so intimately and call you friend and brother. Make us quick to speak your name, and put others on our hearts who need to know who you are and what you've done. May the songs you've given us strengthen us through the day, so that we glory in your holy name and seek your face. We pray in Jesus' name. Amen.
